rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 2.2-2.3 and 3.1-3.3 - the study reports its own one-season (2013) field monitoring of soil water content, maize growth and meteorology in three flood-irrigated maize fields in the Heihe River basin, plus HYDRUS-1D calibration/validation and scenario runs.
rows.notes: The study does not test an app or decision-support scheduling tool; it uses a research hydrodynamic model (HYDRUS-1D) with manual trial-and-error scenario runs to propose optimized schedules, which is not the 'app_scheduling' technology of the claim row. More importantly, the water-conservation effect (irrigation reduced by 13-84%, less deep percolation, Table 2, Section 3.3) comes solely from scenario simulations (OI-1, OI-2) that were never implemented in the field or checked against observations; only the current-schedule SWC simulation was compared with measurements (Fig. 4). Under the rating rules a model result not compared with measurements from the real system does not count as own evidence on the claimed effect. The study does show, under the current schedule, large measured/simulated deep percolation (364, 231 mm in OF and NFD) and Ta/Tp deficits, and authors note limitations (no crop-growth feedback, groundwater feedback not considered, single season) but these cannot be credited because Q2 is no.

notes: Full text appears complete. Single growing season, three fields, one crop; water-saving outcomes are purely scenario-based from a calibrated HYDRUS-1D model.
